newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds stable to higher, retain support.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds stable to higher, retain support.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished flat to higher late Thursday, confounding some players who had anticipated declines after Tuesday's and Wednesday's gains.
"I was slightly surprised at the amount of buyer support there is," said an analyst at a foreign bank.
The market's firmness even flew in the face of lower U.S. Treasuries.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was flat at 90-5/8, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 rose $0.10 to 126.00.
"The market received very well the recent uplifting news which have revived the general level of market activity," said another trader.
"But on the other hand, it is logical that there would be some technical adjustments after the gains of the recent days," he added.
The market got a boost Tuesday and Wednesday from the upgrade of the credit ratings of several Argentine companies by Standard & Poor's.
Call money rates fell to 5.13 percent from 5.38 percent.
